resources.string: Enables lockscreen PIN entry on the physical keyboard, per-app keyboard block, and adaptive keyboard backlight.
Wake screen with a double tap
Type your PIN on hardware keys
Send keys straight to chosen apps
Enter sends, Alt+Enter newline in chat apps
Route number & operator keys to the calculator
Disable Firebase Crashlytics, Analytics and Performance system-wide
Speaker loudness enhancement, on a schedule
Force phone layout on misbehaving apps
Lock screen rotation, globally or per app
Used unless an app below has its own state
Without it, apps that demand portrait or landscape ignore the lock.
%1$d with their own state, of %2$d apps

Locks the screen to one rotation, for every app or for chosen ones. Leaving an app puts the general state back; "System" returns your own auto-rotate setting, restored even if the service restarts. The rotation changes when the app comes to the front, so it can take a moment. Needs root.
Map a spare key to Right Ctrl
Scrolling status-bar banner instead of heads-up
Two-row grid / masonry Overview via LSPosed
Installed %1$s. Restart the app to finish.
pm install failed — check logcat tag Q25TB-Updater
Force-restart SystemUI to apply a pending tweak
Manual fallback for Ticker Notifications if the root grant didn\'t take

Estimated per-app battery use, read directly from the system\'s own power model via root. This works even though the native Settings screen for this device never populates (it additionally requires a full-charge signal this device\'s charging driver never reports) - but for the same reason, these numbers would otherwise accumulate across multiple charge cycles instead of resetting automatically. Stats now auto-reset once charging reaches the threshold set in the ⋮ menu (default 100%), or you can reset manually any time with the reset button.
Automatically reset battery usage stats once charging reaches this level, since this device can\'t detect an actual full charge.
Wireless ADB enabled on port %1$d. Persisted: %2$s.
Wake the device by double-tapping the screen while it\'s off. The Q25 has no hardware gesture-wake, so this runs a small background watchdog that watches the touchscreen and wakes on a double-tap.
DT2W on. Double-tap the off screen to wake.

Type your lockscreen PIN on the physical keyboard. Digits map phone-dialpad style: W E R = 1 2 3, S D F = 4 5 6, Z X C = 7 8 9, Q = 0. Enter confirms, Backspace deletes. No root needed - uses the accessibility service only.
This feature needs the accessibility service enabled.

Intercepts a spare physical key at the hardware driver level and remaps it to Right Ctrl. Because this runs at the OS input layout level, it works everywhere — including terminal emulators, SSH clients, games, and text editors. Re-binds the keyboard driver on apply so changes take effect immediately.
The € / £ / $ key next to Space. Currently mismapped as backtick by the firmware — remapping it to Ctrl doesn\'t affect normal typing.
The right-hand Shift key. Left Shift still works normally for uppercase.
The dedicated recent-apps/task-switcher key. Remapping it to Ctrl means you lose the hardware shortcut for recents.
Focus first text field after keypress

In selected apps, the accessibility service searches for the first editable text input field after your first physical keypress, focuses it, and replays that key so typing can continue without tapping the field first (e.g., in dialers or messaging apps).
Toggle mute, speaker, and keypad in calls
On the Google Phone call screen, use M to mute/unmute, $ to toggle the speaker, and 0–9 to open the dialer keypad. No root required.
Fix screen/keyboard issues from a bad proximity sensor

If the screen is still off a few seconds after a call genuinely ends, force it back on. Safe to leave on - it\'s a no-op if the screen already came back on its own. Deliberately doesn\'t also respawn the keyboard automatically anymore - see below.

A stuck-near proximity sensor after a call has, in practice, also been observed taking the physical keyboard down with it, not just leaving the screen dark - this button covers that case manually. It\'s kept manual rather than automatic on purpose: pairing it with a forced screen wake was found to race the display driver and crash the kernel, so it\'s not run automatically anymore.

Press Ctrl+W, Ctrl+E, or Ctrl+R to pick suggestion 1, 2, or 3 from the physical keyboard\'s candidate strip (BlackBerry Keyboard, Harpocrat, and similar). Only acts when a suggestion is actually showing, so Ctrl+W/E/R still behave normally elsewhere (e.g. closing a browser tab). No root required.
Bluetooth will turn off after %1$d min with nothing connected.
Auto-disable off. Bluetooth stays as you set it.
Turns Bluetooth off after a period with no device connected, so an idle radio can\'t hold the system awake overnight. Connecting earbuds, a watch or a speaker resets the timer.
Location will turn off after %1$d min with no active GPS fix.
Auto-disable off. Location stays as you set it.

Turns Location off after a period with no active GPS fix (navigation, ride-hailing pickup, camera geotag, ...). Background low-power location checks from Google Play services don\'t count as "active" and won\'t keep resetting the timer.
Auto-block enabled. Will run on every boot.
Toggled telemetry off for all detected apps.

Globally forces off Firebase data collection system-wide — Crashlytics, Analytics / Google Analytics, and Performance Monitoring — by holding their persisted opt-out flags. A watchdog re-applies it every few minutes and after every app install, since the SDKs reset the flags on each cold start. Halts background crash-log and analytics packaging and upload, saving mobile data, RAM, and wakeups.
Automatically turns BesLoudness on at the start time and off at the end time every day, without needing the app open.
Toggles the vendor speaker loudness-enhancement DSP stage, the same one behind Settings\' own "Sound Enhancement" screen. Applies immediately, including to whatever\'s already playing.
Automatically turns Extra Dim on at the start time and off at the end time every day, without needing the app open.
Reduces the screen brightness below the system\'s standard minimum level. Perfect for reading in low light and saving battery at night.

In the AOSP/Google Calculator, route physical keys to the calculator buttons: digits (or W E R / S D F / Z X C / Q for 1-9, 0), plus operators - O = +, I = -, A = ×, G = ÷, M = ., U = %, B = !, T/Y = ( ), Sym/Alt toggles scientific mode, Backspace deletes. No root needed - uses the accessibility service only.

In supported chat and messaging apps, press Enter to send the message and Alt+Enter (or Shift+Enter) to add a new line - so a physical Enter posts instead of inserting a linebreak. Works in Messages, WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, Element/Matrix, Mattermost, Wallapop, ChatGPT and Perplexity. No root needed - uses the accessibility service only.

In the selected apps, physical key presses go straight to the app instead of through the keyboard - handy for games. While a selected app is open the IME is switched to a do-nothing passthrough keyboard, then restored on the way out. Needs root.
Ticker Notifications test - this is how a real notification will scroll by
Needs the accessibility service enabled first (see below).
Heads-up popups are disabled while this is on.
Uses each notifying app\'s own icon color, muted to a dark, readable tone.
Monet needs Android 12+; falls back to the fixed color on this device.

Shows a scrolling banner across the top of the screen for new notifications instead of a heads-up popup, and turns heads-up off system-wide while enabled. Needs root to grant notification access, and the accessibility service enabled to draw the banner.
Notification access not granted - the root grant may have failed; toggle off and on again, or check root access on the Info tab.
Proximity sensor is not available on this device.
Opens the OEM\'s raw sensor readout screen for diagnostics. The near/far threshold is fixed in the sensor\'s firmware - there is no exposed calibration control.
A resolution hotkey, and Material You colours for the gesture arrow.

Resolution hotkey (Screen, Per-app display scaling): a key combination steps the whole screen through a list of resolutions and back to the default. Left or right Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Meta plus a letter or digit; default Right Shift + R; short press or held 0.5 s. Off by default.
Edge gestures: the arrow colours can now come from the Material You palette (Android 12+), so they follow your wallpaper.
Both were merged from separate branches and have unit tests; the merged build was not re-tested on the device beyond installing it. On LineageOS, keep Keyboard, BlackBerry keyboard strip on if you use the resolution hotkey: a screen-size change is what used to bring back the full keyboard.

Makes Recents/Overview show two rows of smaller task cards, tablet-style, instead of the stock single row. It runs entirely through an LSPosed hook inside the launcher; this screen only stores the setting and restarts the launcher.

Open your Xposed manager (LSPosed / Vector), enable \"Q25 Toolbox\", tick the launcher (com.android.launcher3) and this app in its scope, then force-stop the launcher. Requires an Xposed framework on KernelSU / APatch / Magisk.

Grid forces the launcher\'s tablet two-row layout for Recents (the home screen and hotseat may shift slightly, since they share the layout profile). Masonry is Grid with staggered tile heights and square corners.
How much of the wallpaper shows through behind the cards. Restarts the launcher to apply.
Export the selected modules\' settings to a JSON file, or restore them from one. Restore merges into your current settings — it never wipes what isn\'t in the file.
This overwrites the selected modules\' current settings with the ones in the file. Modules not in the file are left as they are.
Removes all sources, added/removed/whitelisted domains, and reverts to the bundled default blacklist. This can\'t be undone.
AdBlock isn\'t installed yet. This deploys a systemless-hosts module that overlays /system/etc/hosts with a compiled blacklist.
Reboot required to activate the hosts overlay. Content edits below will apply automatically once you\'ve rebooted.
Domains here are never blocked, even if a source or manual entry includes them.
Q25 Toolbox could not identify your ROM, and some modules depend on it. You can change this later in Settings.
Choose which system the modules should adapt to

While the device is locked, ignores D-pad, Tab, Space and Enter so a keyboard pressed in a pocket cannot move focus onto the emergency-call button. Enter stays active if PIN on keyboard is on. Needs the accessibility service.
Slim List and Masonry open from the physical Recents key. The on-screen navigation button or gesture still opens the stock Overview.
Blur is unavailable right now (the system turns it off, for example in battery saver).
Multiplies the base time and follows the system animation scale (Developer options). 100% matches the system speed.
Enter / pad opens the PIN on the lockscreen

On the lockscreen, Enter and the pad centre always open the PIN pad. Without this, they activate whatever has focus (unlock, network settings, the newest notification). Needs root and the accessibility service.
Tick an app to block its telemetry. Nothing is blocked until you do.
Grid, standalone (two rows, never uses LSPosed)
Stop the Play Store force-updating chosen apps

Detaches chosen apps from the Play Store so it stops updating them against your auto-update setting. Enabling installs the zygisk-detach module (a Zygisk hook on libbinder); pick the apps to detach below. Turning it off disables the module but keeps your detach list. Needs root and Zygisk (Magisk, ReZygisk or Zygisk Next). Installing, enabling or disabling the module takes effect at boot, while list changes apply as soon as Play Store restarts.
Reboot required for the Zygisk hook to pick up this change. You can edit the list now, but detaching only takes effect after the reboot.
Zygisk doesn\'t look enabled. Turn it on (Magisk\'s settings) or install ReZygisk / Zygisk Next, then reboot - the hook can\'t load without it.
Play Store is on Magisk\'s DenyList (enforced), so Zygisk modules aren\'t loaded into it and detaching silently does nothing.
Couldn\'t read the detach list - it may be corrupted. Applying replaces it with your current selection.
Turn on Zygisk Detach above to manage the list.
Zygisk Detach disabled. Reboot to unload the hook. Your detach list is kept.
Applied. %1$d detached; Play Store was stopped so it re-reads the list.
Play Store removed from the DenyList and stopped. It loads the hook the next time it starts.
Screen off at the ear during calls
Turn the screen off at the ear

During a call, turns the screen off when the phone is held to your ear and back on when you move it away. Replaces the system\'s own handling where it fails to blank the screen. It only acts on the handset earpiece (not speakerphone, Bluetooth or a wired headset) and always wakes the screen when the call ends. Needs root and the accessibility service. Android 12 or later.

Wake the device by double-tapping the screen while it is off. The touch controller keeps reporting touches with the screen off, so a small root listener runs only while the screen is off, and wakes the device on a double tap (two taps within about a second). It stops when the screen turns on, so it costs nothing during use. Needs root and the accessibility service. Fast taps are occasionally missed: just tap again.
Grid is using the LSPosed hook (the launcher\'s own Overview).
Grid is using the standalone overlay.
LSPosed hook: working in the launcher.
LSPosed hook: it could not hook this launcher build, so the standalone Grid is used.
LSPosed hook: not seen in the launcher yet. Enable the module for the launcher in LSPosed, then restart the launcher.
Back / Home / Recents from the screen edges
Swipe inward from this edge. Assign an action to the straight, diagonal-up and diagonal-down swipes, each as a plain swipe or held.
Swipe up from the bottom edge, plain or held.

Each zone is independent. A custom strip is a thin invisible window that takes the touches landing on it, so a tap there does not reach the app below: keep it thin, or switch the zone off. Strips are not active on the lockscreen. There is no system gesture option: the Q25\'s LineageOS does not enable system gesture navigation.
Launcher hook: running. The native bottom swipe-up is switched off while the bottom strip is on.

Launcher hook: not seen yet. The bottom strip needs it, or the native swipe-up fires too. Enable the Q25 Toolbox module for the launcher in LSPosed and restart the launcher, then touch the screen and check again.
This motor has no amplitude control: only the duration changes the feel.
The strips are switched off while one of these apps is in front (games, drawing apps, anything that needs the screen edges).
Show the round badge (off = bare arrow)
Arrow turns with the finger direction
Copy these settings to the right edge
Copy these settings to the left edge
Switch off the native bottom gesture
The launcher\'s own swipe-up (home / recents / quick switch). Needed for the bottom strip, or both fire. Works through the LSPosed module, with no strip required.
Leave the Recents key to another app (Key Mapper)

The key stays remapped, so Android does nothing with it, but this app stops acting on it. Key Mapper then sees it as PROG_RED (keycode 183, scancode 580, any device): make the trigger with that key and set the short, double and long presses there. To open this app\'s Recents overlay from Key Mapper use the action Send intent, type Broadcast, with the component com.kgr.q25toolbox / com.kgr.q25toolbox.service.RunActionReceiver, and no extras (the default is the Recents overlay). The extra action with a value such as PREVIOUS_APP, HOME, NOTIFICATIONS or FLASHLIGHT runs another action of Edge Gestures. Needs the accessibility service, and is ignored on the lockscreen.
Keep the keyboard on its suggestions strip (LineageOS)

The BlackBerry keyboard sometimes shows its full on-screen keyboard instead of the strip. Cause (from its code and Android\'s): it targets an old SDK, so on this square screen Android hands it a configuration with the status bar taken off the height, which reads as landscape, and it shows the full keyboard when it thinks the screen is landscape. This turns on Android\'s per-app switch OVERRIDE_ENABLE_INSETS_DECOUPLED_CONFIGURATION for the keyboard only, so it gets the display\'s own (portrait) configuration. No Xposed needed. Turning it on or off restarts the keyboard for a moment.
Active: the keyboard gets the display\'s portrait configuration.
Off: the keyboard still gets the legacy configuration.
Keeps the suggestions strip instead of the full keyboard
Material You colours (pick a family, then a shade)
Follows your wallpaper. Pick another colour to stop.

A key combination that switches the whole screen to a resolution and, pressed again, back to the default. With several resolutions, each press goes to the next one and the press after the last returns to the default. It overrides the per-app targets until you step back.
Add a resolution to switch to.

The press is consumed here, but other accessibility apps (Key Mapper) still see it: if you bound the same combination there, both act, so delete those. With the long press, a quick tap is swallowed too; the switch above types it again on release, slightly late, so fast typing right after it could arrive out of order. Not active on the lockscreen. The screen stays at the chosen resolution after it turns off, and returns to the default if the accessibility service restarts.
A quick tap types the key (re-sent as a key combination, about 75 ms late; needs root)
